author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read NinjaOne activity webhook deliveries, each an Activity object from NinjaOne's public API schema. The activity webhook posts straight to HTTP Ingest. Console logins, logouts and MFA changes go to Auth; scripts, actions and remote access go to ManagementEvent; triggered conditions and antivirus threat activities go to the third-party alert schema; the rest stays generic.
notes:
Setup:
- NinjaOne has no syslog export for activities.
- Configure its activity webhook (PUT /v2/webhook in the Public API, or the SIEM Exporter app) with a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest URL, the header Authorization: Bearer <integration key>, the activity types you want and the device expansion; README.md has an example body.

Field mapping:
- Each delivery is an Activity object from NinjaOne's public API schema.
- Console logins, logouts, failed logins and MFA changes go to Auth; scripts and actions, remote access, remote tools, credential access and technician role changes go to ManagementEvent; triggered conditions and antivirus threat activities go to the third-party alert schema; the rest stays generic.
- NinjaOne doesn't document the wording of subject and message, so the user is the first email address in them (else userId) and the source address is the first IPv4 address in the message; check both against a real delivery.

Time:
- Event times keep whole seconds.

Sources and licenses:
- activityType and statusCode values come from the API schema.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the Activity schema.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 (112 of 112 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.
